_comment: Suite wall-clock ceilings (#656 Layer 5). Tighten-only, ratcheted alongside the perf budgets in scripts/test-report/ratchet-floors.mjs. `budgetMs` is the sum of per-file durations in artifacts/test-results/vitest.json, not the run's elapsed time — elapsed varies with host load and --concurrency, while the sum is the work the suite actually asked for, which is what an added test increases. Seeded 2026-07-31 from a full `bun run coverage` on this branch: 849 files, 1,408.3s measured, ceiling set 15% above at 1,620,000ms. Widening this number needs a top-level `approvedDeviation` saying what the extra time buys; `bun run test:suite-wall-clock -- --write` only ever lowers it.
approvedDeviation: #839 + #842 widen `pr-vitest` from 1,620,000ms to 1,825,000ms. WHAT THE EXTRA TIME BUYS: the two umbrellas add the adversary lanes the suite did not have — the seeded fuzz runner and crasher replay, the protocol join lane, the time zoo, network and composition chaos, the crash-consistency kill lane, the backup-format and schema-migration corpora, the prompt-injection corpus, the hostile-peer harness, the handler sandbox and its confinement suites, and the differential guard corpus. The file count goes 849 -> 1332 (+57%) and the ceiling had never been re-seeded, so it was measuring a suite that no longer exists: this branch is the first time the gate has ever run in CI at all (W0.1 wired it; before that the ceiling shipped with #656 and no lane invoked it). MEASURED 2026-08-22 at 1,587.1s over 1,332 files by a full local `bun run coverage`, and the new ceiling is 15% above that — the same method and the same margin the 2026-07-31 seed used. The margin is what absorbs a CI runner being slower than this host, which is precisely how the old number came to be red: CI's sum crossed 1,620s while the same tree measured 1,587s locally. This is a re-seed against a deliberately larger suite, not slack for a slower one — `--write` still only ever lowers the number, and the next sustained measurement should ratchet it back down.
